title: Ozito PXC 36V (2x18V) 410mm Brushless Lawn Mower Kit $229 @ Bunnings Warehouse (In-Store)
body:

[anthman] The one to get is the steel deck version for $399. So this is a good price if you don't mind the plastic construction
[bargaino] The plastic is quite rugged. Just don't leave it out in the sun between uses.
[Mokr] Steel deck is bigger but isn't it heaver to move so a slower mow if you have a curvy lwan

[Jimothy Wongingtons] I rate the steel deck one, actually really happy with it coming from a petrol Ryobi that served me well for basically 10 years
[garage sale] Seasonal promo, not regular stock item , so once Bunnings clear their warehouse, that’s it for this summer for this mower.
[pinchies] Looks like a new line, the PDF manual creation date is 8/17/26.
URL should be https://www.bunnings.com.au/_p1108457 but not showing yet on bunnings site or on YIS.
Good price if $229 is the actual price… the 370mm dual 18V mower at Aldi was $250.
[Rochie] Been holding out for one of the steel deck ones to go on sale again but 410mm is big enough if this becomes available.
[tenpercent] I thought you had said something about Ozito in another discussion. Thought you might be interested. Maybe I misread. Sorry if that's the case.

.

[Series4Episode10] Can't speak for Ozito rubbish, but you'd think, my 2x18v battery Makita chainsaw is way more powerful than my old single battery Makita model of the same bar length.
[Doineedthis] Hmm this is cheaper than buying new batteries for my 8yo aeg mower. Tempted to go the self propelled version as my lawn is a bit bumpy. Anyone tried it?
[Captain Yobbo] Regular steel deck one is fine even if you have a bit of a gradient, it's obviously heavier but not to the point it's a burden.
[Series4Episode10] Having some old Ozito tools still holding on way past the rest of the stuff in the Ozito kit I bought in 2019 - Ozito batteries are way less energy dense and fail at a rate far quicker than my Makita stuff - in fact not one of those Ozito batteries that came with the kit originally lasted long at all, bought a 4 piece Makita set having learnt my lesson buying cheap crap, purchased in 2020 after buying a property, every one of those 3 batteries is still good (2 included and 1 by redemption)
.
I've bought several packs of Ozito batteries over that time to keep using those tools and a Ozito vacuum cleaner that's really good and right now I only have 1 working Ozito battery, NOT worth the $, cost of ownership WAY to high, set up an alert on Ebay for for your branded batteries, I often get $100 Makita 5ah batteries of a guy (ryde tools or something like that) who must be buying the sets when they come up cheap and selling off the individual pieces.
[tunzafun001] 4.0ah batteries seem a bit small for a mower?
What's the avg run time on a biweekly trim of kykuku lawn?
Will it cut through a neglected lawn? (I normally cut the neighbors after a couple of months before the weeds seed and head our way).
*Still 700m2 minimum blocks here.. so lawns are actual old school "lawns ". 15 -20min to cut normally (no catcher/ no stopping).
